claims.claim_text: 加速來自四種 dispatch 模式（direct-threaded、indirect-threaded、switch-loop、call-loop）

claims.claim_text: （原文）CoreMark 從 1.0 的約 2800 分推到約 4200 分
claims.evidence: After applying the fix to Wasmi 2.0 its CoreMark score rose from ~2800 to over 4200. That's a ~50% improvement with this singular fix which made it the single most important "optimization" for Wasmi 2.0.
claims.note: 來源的 ~2800→4200 是 Wasmi 2.0 套用 Rust 1.92 DestinationPropagation 修正前後的對比，不是 Wasmi 1.0 對 2.0。FIXED：改寫為「單一影響最大的改動其實來自 Rust 1.92 的 DestinationPropagation 修正，光是這一項就把 Wasmi 2.0 自己的 CoreMark 分數從約 2800 推到 4200 以上」。

claims.claim_text: 作者給的定位是「the fastest portable Wasm interpreters」這一級
claims.evidence: Wasmi 2.0 clearly belongs to the category of the fastest portable Wasm interpreters.

claims.claim_text: 把值留在硬體暫存器而非 stack slot 的 accumulator register、改成連續佈局的 instance 存取，以及能把函式指標烘進 bytecode 的 lock-free code map
claims.evidence: Wasmi 2.0 introduces three hardware register accumulators (ireg, freg32, freg64) to store intermediate results directly in CPU registers rather than stack slots … The new contiguous InstanceEntity layout places all instance objects in a single memory allocation … Functions now bake directly into bytecode as pointers, using append-only bucket allocation that never reallocates, enabling concurrent lock-free access across all instances sharing module bytecode.

claims.claim_text: 發現 Rust 的 compiler-builtins 與 musl libc 都「fail to properly handle rounding for subnormals」
claims.evidence: fail to properly handle rounding for subnormals

claims.claim_text: Rust 端是 issue #1262 配 PR #1270 … 另有一個影響 32-bit ARM 上 f128 的 rustc ABI bug 記在 issue #1271
claims.evidence: Issue #1262: Rust standard library's f32::mul_add bug report; PR #1270: fix for Rust compiler-builtins; Issue #1271: rustc ABI bug affecting f128 type on 32-bit ARM platforms
a = 0x97000800, b = 0x1cfff001, c = 0x00010002 … should produce 0x00010001 (correct) but instead yields 0x00010002

claims.claim_text: musl 那份實作源出 2005 到 2011 年的 FreeBSD，同一個 subnormal 缺陷可能早已散進大量嵌入式工具鏈。
claims.evidence: musl libc references FreeBSD code (copyright 2005-2011) containing the same flaw … copy-pasted over the past two decades

claims.evidence: Encoding operates at 4.31 nanoseconds per byte (~232 MB/s), incurred once during cache insertion; Decoding runs at 1.56 nanoseconds per byte (~641 MB/s), applied on every retrieval

claims.claim_text: 在測試流量下額外 CPU 只有「a few percent」

claims.claim_text: Cloudflare 在 Pingora 裡把進 cache 的資源先用 zstd level 3 編碼再落盤，送給 client 時才解開，跨資料中心走 Tiered Cache 的期間也維持壓縮狀態。
claims.evidence: The system leverages Zstandard at level 3 within Pingora's proxy architecture. When content enters the cache, it's compressed; the compressed version persists across Tiered Cache transfers between data centers. Crucially, the system decompresses responses before delivery to clients.

claims.claim_text: 把讀流量切到 replica 之後，作者的測試裡有 99.2% 的近期寫入讀不到
claims.evidence: The replica is on the same machine as its primary and talks to it over loopback, and naive reads still miss 99.2% of the time.

claims.claim_text: PostgreSQL 19 的 WAIT FOR LSN 讓 standby 阻塞到追上指定位置：commit 後在 primary 用 pg_current_wal_flush_lsn() 取位置存下來，讀之前在 replica 執行 WAIT FOR LSN 並帶上 MODE 'standby_replay' 與 TIMEOUT。
claims.evidence: WAIT FOR LSN '0/554D1B78' WITH (MODE 'standby_replay', TIMEOUT '5ms', NO_THROW) … SELECT pg_current_wal_flush_lsn()

claims.claim_text: 1,000 次測試裡 stale read 歸零
claims.evidence: the "WAIT FOR, then read replica" row achieved zero stale reads out of 1,000 tests

claims.claim_text: （原文）代價是每次讀多約 1 ms
claims.evidence: one to two milliseconds slower than going to the primary at every percentile
claims.note: 來源寫的是 one to two milliseconds slower ... at every percentile，post 收窄成「約 1 ms」。FIXED：改為「各個百分位上都比直接走 primary 慢一到兩毫秒」。

claims.claim_text: 而且等待中的連線會一直佔著 pool，lag 全面拉高時流量會整批倒回 primary。
claims.evidence: Waiting readers hold database connections for their entire timeout duration. During cluster-wide lag events, this can exhaust connection pools precisely when load spikes most dangerously. … Mass timeouts redirect traffic back to the primary simultaneously, potentially overwhelming it with concentrated load.
